Enarrationes in Job
ΩΡΙΓΕΝΟΥΣ ΕΞΗΓΗΤΙΚΑ ΕΙΣ ΤΟΝ ΙΩΒ.
17.57 ΚΕΦ. Αʹ. Στίχ. ιʹ. Οὐ σὺ περιέφραξας τὰ ἔξω αὐτοῦ; Πόθεν οἶδας, ὅτι πέφρακται;
Οὗτος ὁ ἀντίδικος ἡμῶν ὁ διάβολος ὡς λέων ὠρυόμενος περιπορεύε 17.60 ται, ζητῶν
καταπιεῖν τινα. Ἦλθεν οὖν καὶ περὶ τὸν Ἰὼβ, βουλόμενος τὰ αὐτὰ ποιῆσαι. Ὕστερον
λαβὼν ἐξουσίαν, ταῦτα πεποίηκε. Καὶ ὅτι πάντα πε ριπεφραγμένα ἦν, καὶ ταῦτα
νοήσας ἐκ τοῦ κεκωλύ σθαι· βουλόμενος ποιεῖν τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰὼβ, εἶπε· Σὺ
περιέφραξας τὰ ἔσω αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ ἔξω αὐτοῦ. Πάν τα οὖν ἐφ' ὅσον οὐ δίδοται τῷ
διαβόλῳ, σὺ περιέ φραξας. Στ. ιηʹ. Ἔτι τούτου λαλοῦντος, ἄλλος ἄγγελος λέγων τῷ
Ἰώβ· Τῶν υἱῶν σου καὶ τῶν θυγατέ ρων σου ἐσθιόντων καὶ πινόντων, παρὰ τῷ ἀδελ
φῷ αὐτῶν τῷ πρεσβυτέρῳ, Στ. ιθʹ. Ἐξαίφνης πνεῦμα μέγα ἐπῆλθεν ἐκ τῆς ἐρήμου,
καὶ ἥψατο τῶν τεσσάρων γωνιῶν τῆς οἰκίας, καὶ ἔπεσεν ἡ οἰκία ἐπὶ τὰ παιδία σου,
καὶ ἐτελεύτησαν. Ἐσώθην δὲ ἐγὼ μόνος, καὶ ἦλθον τοῦ ἀπαγγεῖλαί σοι. Τὰς μὲν οὖν
καμήλους πεποίηκε γενέσθαι ὑπὸ τοὺς ἱππεῖς, τοὺς ὄνους δὲ καὶ τὰ ζεύγη τῶν βοῶν
ὑπὸ τοὺς αἰχμαλωτίζοντας· τὰ πρόβατα δὲ ἐμίσει. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο πῦρ ἐπ' αὐτὰ κατήγαγεν.
Ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς ἐπεβούλευσε, καιρὸν ἐζήτει τοῦ αὐτοὺς ἀπολέ σαι. Εἰ εὑρήκει
ἀναγινώσκοντας, οὐκ ἂν ἥψατο τῆς οἰκίας, οὐδὲ τόπον εἶχε τοῦ αὐτοὺς ἀποκτεῖναι.
Εἰ εὑρήκει προσευχομένους, οὐδὲν ἠδύνατο ποιῆσαι κατ' αὐτῶν. Ἀλλ' ὅτε εὗρεν
εὐκαιρίαν, ἴσχυσε. Ποῖος οὖν ὁ καιρός; Μέθη ἦν, συμπόσιον ἦν. Τὸ, τῶν γω νιῶν τῆς
οἰκίας ἅψασθαι τὸ πνεῦμα, ἐπίστησον, ὅτι ἐν ταῖς τῶν γωνιῶν πλατείαις οἱ
ὑποκριταὶ ἑστῶτες προσεύχονται· πᾶς δὲ ὁ μὴ ἐπιβεβηκὼς εὐθείας ὁδοῦ, ταῖς γωνίαις
κέχρηται. Πλατεῖα δὲ γωνία ἡ πολλὴ καὶ ἀνειμένη κακία. ΚΕΦ. Βʹ. Στίχ. βʹ. Καὶ εἶπεν
ὁ Κύριος τῷ διαβόλῳ· Πό θεν σὺ ἔρχῃ; Ἑώρα ὁ Θεὸς, ὅπως αἰσχυνθεὶς διεπονεῖτο ὁ
Σατα νᾶς. Ὅταν δὲ ἐπερωτῶν ἴδῃ ἀγνωμονοῦντα, τότε ἐλέγχει κακουργοῦντα, ὡς
ἤλεγξε τὸν Κάϊν. Στ. θʹ. Χρόνου δὲ προβεβηκότος, εἶπεν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ. Ὅρα τὸ
κακοῦργον. Ὅτε πολὺς διῆλθε χρόνος, τότε ἐπιτίθεται· τότε γὰρ μάλιστα τῆς
δυνάμεως ἐξασθε νεῖ. ∆ιπλᾶ τὰ τῆς ἀσθενείας ἦν, τῷ τε τὸν φέροντα ἀσθενέστερον
γενέσθαι τῷ μήκει τοῦ χρόνου, καὶ τῷ τὴν ἐλπίδα ἀπογνωσθῆναι μᾶλλον. Καὶ μετ'
ὀλίγα· Μὴ τοίνυν τοῦτο ἴδωμεν, ὅτι γυνὴ, ἀλλὰ τί συμβου λεύει. Τοῦτο καὶ τοῖς νῦν
ἀνθρώποις παραινῶ, μὴ πρὸς τὰ τῶν προσώπων ἀξιώματα βλέπειν, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὸν
τρόπον τῆς συμβουλῆς. Γυνή ἐστιν ἵνα βοηθῇ, οὐχ ἵνα ὑποσκελίζῃ. Στ. θʹ. Εἶπεν αὐτῷ
ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ· Μέχρι τί νος καρτερήσεις; Τὸ πάντων μηχανημάτων τῶν
προλαβόντων ἰσχυ ρότερον ὕστερον ὁ διάβολος προσάγει. Εἴθε καὶ ταύ την ἔλαβες!
Εἴθε μετὰ τῶν παίδων κατέχωσας! Τινὲς δέ φασιν οὐδὲ τῆς γυναικὸς εἶναι τὰ
ῥήματα, ἀλλ' αὐ 17.61 τὸν εἰς αὐτὴν τυπωθέντα ταῦτα φθέγγεσθαι· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἦν τὴν
γυναῖκα τοῦ Ἰὼβ τοιαύτην εἶναι· πλὴν εἴ τις λέγοι, συμφορᾷ περιτραπεῖσαν,
τοιαύτην αὐτὴν γενέ σθαι. Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα· Εἰκὸς οὐ ταύτην πρώτην γε γενῆσθαι τὴν
συμβουλὴν, ἀλλὰ πολλάκις πολλὰ τού των ἀκοῦσαι χαλεπώτερα παρὰ τῆς γυναικός.
Ὅρα διαβολικὴν ἀπάτην. Ἐνενόησε τὴν Εὔαν. Τοῦτο, φησὶ, τὸν πρῶτον κατήνεγκεν
ἄνθρωπον· τοῦτο καὶ τούτου περιγενέσθαι δυνήσεται. Ἀλλ', ὦ ἄθλιε καὶ ἀνόητε!
ἐκεῖνον ἥττονα γαστρὸς εὑροῦσα, ἰὸν ἔσπειρε τὸν ἑαυ τῆς. Τοῦτον δὲ ὁρᾷς
φιλοσοφοῦντα, καὶ αὐτῆς περι γενόμενον τῆς φύσεως. Οὐκ ἐπέκαμψεν αὐτὸν χρη
μάτων ἀπώλεια, οὐδὲ παίδων θάνατος ἄωρος, οὐδὲ βάσανος σώματος
ἀπαραμύθητος, οὐδὲ χρόνου μῆκος τοσοῦτον. Καὶ τὸν ὑπὸ πραγμάτων οὐχ ἁλόντα,
τοῦ τον ὑπὸ λόγων προσδοκᾷς χειρώσασθαι; Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. Τί τὸν ἀθλητὴν ἐκλύεις; Τί
καταστέλλεις τὰς χεῖ ρας; δέον εἰπεῖν κατὰ τὸν Ἀπόστολον· Ἔτι μικρὸν, ἔτι μικρόν.
Στ. θʹ. Ἀλλ' εἶπόν τι ῥῆμα εἰς Κύριον, καὶ τελεύτα. Μετὰ τὸ τὴν τραγῳδίαν ἀκριβῶς
pass_a_gloss: Of Origen, exegetical things on Job. Chapter 1, verse 10. Did you not fence round the things outside him? From where do you know that it has been fenced? This adversary of ours, the devil, goes about like a roaring lion, seeking to swallow someone. So he came also around Job, wanting to do the same things. Later, having taken authority, he did these things. And that all things had been fenced round, he understood this also from his having been hindered; wanting to do the things concerning Job, he said: You fenced round the things inside him and the things outside him. So all things, in so far as it is not given to the devil, you fenced round. Verse 18. While this one was still speaking, another messenger saying to Job: While your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking beside their elder brother, verse 19, suddenly a great wind came upon from the desert, and touched the four corners of the house, and the house fell upon your children, and they died. And I alone was saved, and I came to report to you. The camels, then, he made to come under the horsemen, and the donkeys and the yokes of the oxen under those taking captive; but the sheep he hated. Because of this he brought fire down upon them. But he also plotted against the sons; he was seeking a moment for destroying them. If he had found them reading, he would not have touched the house, nor would he have had a place for killing them. If he had found them praying, he could do nothing against them. But when he found an opportunity, he was strong. What then was the moment? It was drunkenness, it was a drinking party. The phrase, the wind touched the corners of the house, pay attention, that in the broad places of the corners the hypocrites standing pray; and every one who has not stepped onto a straight road has made use of the corners. And a broad corner is the much and slackened wickedness. Chapter 2, verse 2. And the Lord said to the devil: From where do you come? God saw how, having been put to shame, Satan was being worked up in distress. And when, questioning, he sees him being unreasonable (ungrateful), then he convicts him doing evil, as he convicted Cain. Verse 9. And time having advanced, his wife said to him. See the evil-working thing. When much time passed through, then he sets upon; for then most of all one grows weak in strength. Double were the things of the weakness: both in the bearer having become weaker by the length of the time, and in the hope having been despaired of more. And after a few things: Let us not then see this, that she is a woman (wife), but what she counsels. This I exhort also to the people now, not to look to the dignities of the persons, but to the manner of the counsel. A woman (wife) is in order that she may help, not in order that she may trip up. Verse 9. His wife said to him: Until when will you endure? The device stronger than all the devices that went before, the devil brings forward later. Would that you had taken this one too! Would that you had buried her with the children! But some say that the words are not even of the woman, but that he, having been shaped into her, utters these things; for it was not possible for the wife of Job to be such; except if someone should say that, overturned by calamity, she became such. And after a few things: It is likely that this counsel had not come to be the first, but that he often heard many things harder than these from the woman. See devilish deceit. He had in mind Eve. This, he says, brought down the first human; this will be able to prevail also over this one. But, O wretched and senseless one! She, having found that one lesser than the belly, sowed her own poison. But this one you see philosophizing, and having prevailed over nature itself. Loss of goods did not bend him, nor untimely death of children, nor torment of body without consolation, nor so great a length of time. And him who was not caught by events, do you expect to subdue by words? Of the same. Why do you loosen the athlete? Why do you put down the hands? when it was necessary to say according to the Apostle: Yet a little, yet a little. Verse 9. But say some word against the Lord, and die. After the tragedy exactly ... (the infinitive to recount follows in the next section).
pass_b_english: “Have you not fenced round what is outside him?” (Job 1:10). How do you know that it has been fenced? This is our adversary the devil, who goes about like a roaring lion, seeking someone to swallow (1 Peter 5:8). So he came round Job too, wanting to do the same things to him. Later, once he had received authority, he did them. That everything was fenced round he understood from the very fact that he had been held back; and since he wanted to do his work on Job, he said: “You have fenced round what is inside him and what is outside him.” Everything, then, so far as it is not handed over to the devil, you have fenced round.

“While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job: While your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking at the house of their elder brother, suddenly a great wind came from the desert and struck the four corners of the house, and the house fell on your children, and they died. I alone escaped, and I have come to tell you” (Job 1:18-19). The camels, then, he made fall to the horsemen, and the donkeys and the yokes of oxen to the raiders; but the sheep he hated, and that is why he brought fire down on them. He laid a plot against the sons as well, and kept looking for a moment to destroy them. If he had found them reading, he would not have touched the house, nor would he have had any opening to kill them. If he had found them praying, he could have done nothing against them. But when he found his opportunity, he prevailed. What, then, was the opportunity? There was drunkenness; there was a drinking party. Notice the words “the wind struck the corners of the house”: it is in the broad places of the corners that the hypocrites stand and pray (Matthew 6:5), and everyone who has not set foot on the straight road makes use of corners. A broad corner is wickedness that is great and unbridled.

“And the Lord said to the devil: Where do you come from?” (Job 2:2). God saw how Satan, put to shame, was in torment. And whenever, on questioning someone, God sees him acting without good sense, then he convicts the evildoer, as he convicted Cain.

“When time had gone on, his wife said to him” (Job 2:9). See the villainy. When a long time had gone by, that is when he attacks; for that is when strength is at its weakest. The weakness was twofold: the man bearing the trials had grown weaker through the length of time, and his hope had been given up all the more.

And a little later: Let us not, then, look at the fact that she is his wife, but at what she advises. This I urge on people today as well: do not look at the rank of the persons, but at the kind of counsel they give. A wife exists to help, not to trip up.

“His wife said to him: How long will you hold out?” (Job 2:9). The device stronger than all the devices before it, the devil brings up last. Would that you had taken her too! Would that you had buried her with the children! Some say that the words were not even the woman's, but that he himself, having shaped himself into her, was uttering them; for it was not possible for Job's wife to be such a woman, unless one were to say that she became such after being overturned by calamity.

And a little later: It is likely that this was not the first time this counsel had been given, but that he had often heard many things harsher than these from his wife. See the devilish deceit. He thought of Eve. “This,” he says, “brought down the first man; this will be able to get the better of this man too.” But, you wretched and senseless one! She found that man weaker than his belly and sowed her own venom; but this man you see living as a philosopher and mastering nature itself. The loss of his goods did not bend him, nor the untimely death of his children, nor the comfortless torture of his body, nor so long a stretch of time. The man whom events did not capture, do you expect to subdue with words?
From the same: Why do you unnerve the athlete? Why do you pull down his hands? You ought to have said, as the Apostle does: “Yet a little while, yet a little while” (Hebrews 10:37).
“But say some word against the Lord, and die” (Job 2:9). After the tragedy has been exactly …

choices.choice: ΩΡΙΓΕΝΟΥΣ ΕΞΗΓΗΤΙΚΑ ΕΙΣ ΤΟΝ ΙΩΒ rendered once as 'Origen's Expository Notes on Job'; the Latin header 'Enarrationes in Job' is a file label and is not rendered.
ΚΕΦ./Στίχ. labels appear only as the reference after each quoted lemma, KJV numbering checked by the words; no translator headings.
Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα → 'And a little later:'; Τοῦ αὐτοῦ → 'From the same:'; each opens its own paragraph.
Τοῦτο καὶ τοῖς νῦν ἀνθρώποις παραινῶ kept as 'This I urge on people today as well'.
Kept as an exclamation addressed in the second person, as the Greek has it; no addressee supplied.
Ends with '…' where the Greek breaks off (Μετὰ τὸ τὴν τραγῳδίαν ἀκριβῶς); the verb follows in u01-rem-early.
